intervals.label: deployment and first season
intervals.note: Deployed in the 2014-2015 austral summer (LAMBDA); the 2016 paper calls 2016 "its second year of observation (and first science season)", so the commissioning end is set at 2016 (year precision).

physics_goals.quote: BICEP3 is a 520 mm aperture, compact two-lens refractor designed to observe the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at 95 GHz.
physics_goals.value: Observe the CMB polarization at 95 GHz, the foreground minimum, to constrain inflationary gravitational waves.

summary.plain: The successor to BICEP2: a larger 95 GHz telescope with 2560 detectors in a South Pole laboratory. Its maps, with Keck Array data, give the strongest limit on gravitational waves from inflation.
summary.technical: 95 GHz refracting CMB polarimeter (520 mm aperture, 2560 TES bolometers) at the South Pole, deployed 2014-15, science observations since 2016; its maps dominate the BICEP/Keck BK18 constraint r_0.05 < 0.036 (95%).
